about: Ground the world stands bodies on. Absent `ground` option = the flat floor of world.json, unchanged. Every number names its source. Nothing is hard-coded in src/ground.mjs.

flat.source: world.json floor row (same box, same friction): angle 0 builds the identical body, so its per-tick hash equals the default floor

slope15.source: Strategy 2026-10-28 (V3 terrain: hills and ridges): gentle slope; friction = world.json floor

slope30.source: Strategy 2026-10-28 (V3 terrain): steep ridge; friction = world.json floor. tan(30) = 0.577 is under friction 0.8, so a resting rigid body holds (the angle that starts sliding is atan(0.8) = 38.7)

plane.source: world.json floor box: half-height 0.5, convex radius 0.05. max_angle_deg: own, a slope steeper than 60 is a wall, not ground

continuous.source: own: sampled ground (heightfield, mesh) is a thin shell, so a small fast body can jump through it in one tick (reviewer: a 0.03 m sphere dropped from 1 m, a 0.13 m sphere at 12 m/s, ragdolls from 2 to 4 m went 0.15 to 0.5 m deep). With ground set, ragdoll parts and props are created with Jolt linear-cast (continuous) motion. max_drop_m: the highest spawn above groundMax that the tunnel test proves; createRagdoll and createProp throw above it. Plane rows are a solid 1 m box and keep the default motion (so the flat row stays hash-identical to the default floor); the drop limit applies to every ground.

roll.source: own: a cut piece or prop on a non-default ground loses spin at coefficient x g / radius rad/s^2 while its lowest point is within contact_m of the surface. A severed head or limb is not a smooth cylinder, so it resists rolling about like a block resists sliding: coefficient = the floor friction 0.8 (world.json). Holds a piece still while sin(angle) < 0.8, i.e. under 53 degrees. Measured before this row: a dog head cut on slope15 rolled 43 m in 12 s and never stopped (VPS, 2026-10-28)

probe.source: own: groundMax looks at the centre and 8 points around the footprint circle; enough for a hill whose features are wider than a body

sampled.source: own: a sampled height function `groundHeight(x, z)` from the game, one sample per cell_m over the same 100 m square as the floor, built as a Jolt HeightFieldShape (compact: 1 byte per sample, no triangle list, good for the phone). shape "mesh" builds a Jolt triangle mesh from the same samples (float heights, about 20 bytes per triangle) when exact heights matter more than memory. Measured on the VPS: a sphere resting on a sampled 15 degree plane sits within 1.1 mm of the surface for both shapes (quantisation is per block, not per field). friction = world.json floor

settle.drop_height_source: own: spawn the body this far above the highest ground under its footprint, so it lands on its own weight
settle.footprint_source: own: radius searched for the highest ground under the spawn (arms out / dog length)
settle.max_settle_source: own: ragdolls on the flat floor freeze inside 15 s (test/chain-dog-drone.test.mjs steps 15 s); a slope gets 20 s
settle.clearance_source: KNOWN DEFECT, not a pass: sink_epsilon_m 0.11 hides a real toe-capsule sink (0.072 m into the default flat floor, 0.021 m on plane rows, 0.105 m into the slope15 heightfield: margin to the 0.11 limit is only 0.005 m). Open, owner: physics. float: Jolt's penetration slop 0.02 m plus 0.01 m for float32 poses and triangle interpolation. sink: measured, and NOT ground-specific: a killed vagrant-106's toe capsule sinks into the DEFAULT flat floor by up to 0.072 m over ten drop heights (baseline test), into a sampled heightfield/mesh by up to 0.105 m (slope15, drop 0.4; VPS 2026-10-28: limp ragdoll under its own weight, a thin toe capsule). 0.11 = the worst measured plus rounding. Real tunnelling through the ground is 0.3 m or more, which this still catches
settle.hold_source: own: once asleep a body must not move at all over 5 s (a sleeping body is not stepped); 1 mm is float32 noise
settle.max_slide_source: own: a limp body that lands on a 30 degree slope may roll and slide, but must stop inside the runway; measured on the VPS, see the PR body
